entries.title: Guidestone Translation
entries.text:
Jacquelyn has instructed me that she would feel safer if I moved the translation key offline. The woman is paranoid, but I don't disagree that it's for good reason. It is because of this that she insists on keeping the original notes with her. She says it's for the best, just in case someone gets to one of us, so none of us have all the pieces. Even Agent Wilson's taking precautions. We could be onto something big here.

Then again... I still maintain the runes are simply ancient petroglyphs left by the indigenous peoples of the region. Jacquelyn believes they may be extraterrestrial in nature, but I'll stick with Occam on this one. The hypothesis with the fewest assumptions is often the correct one.

entries.title: Horse Creek Petroglyphs
entries.text:
Had a chance to go study the Horse Creek Petroglyphs in person. I've been meaning to do so ever since moving to West Virginia. They have always fascinated me. The idea that Europeans landed in North America and travelled that far inland during the sixth or seventh century is fascinating. Now, whether it was written in Old Irish Ogham, Basque, or some other ancient language is up for debate. 

Personally, I prefer the Basque translation, as it paints a vivid picture of a great bison hunt. But regardless, it's exciting to study and theorize about any petroglyphs in our own back yard.

entries.title: Jacquelyn
entries.text: Jacquelyn brought more of her notes around the other day. Still not sure what to make of those runes. They don't match any of the native petroglyphs in the area,  nor do they match any of the old European runes I would have expected. Still, I'm confident I will find a match somewhere, and if not there may be enough to go on to piece together a rough idea of what they say, if anything. I'm beginning to think it may be nonsense, but I am intrigued.

entries.title: VTU
entries.text: Ever since Vault-Tec bought out the University, they've been shifting focus away from classic education and moving towards more specialized classes. I've seen several other professors get the boot, but thankfully, I seem to have been spared thus far. I should feel lucky that they believe language is a skill worth preserving in the event society collapses and we all need to move underground.

items.name: Young Dweller Development Terminal
items.lead: A terminal you can read in the world.

entries.title: Introduction
entries.text:
One of the duties of a Vault Overseer may involve becoming a surrogate parent or dispensing advice to actual parents of young dwellers. 

Through this series of courses, Vault-Tec will instruct you on how to deal with one of the most difficult classifications of children, the preteen (10 to 12 years of age). If you have any questions about the entries in this syllabus, please speak to a Vault-Tec University representative.

entries.title: VTU-PDM101
entries.text:
VTU-PDM101 - Introduction to Preteen Dweller Maintenance

This course is designed to introduce the mechanics of preteen physiology. The focus will be primarily regarding maintenance and upkeep, including things that can go wrong in the preteen's body.

Students will be instructed how to repair common issues and deal with physiological emergencies. Please note that this course includes laboratory dissection work, so the proper biohazard equipment will be issued after registration is completed.

entries.title: VTU-PDM201
entries.text:
VTU-PDM201 - Introduction to Preteen Psychology

Preteens feature the most complex psychology of any age group. This course will equip the Vault Overseer with the proper armament to handle an array of preteen psychological issues that may arise within their Vaults. 

Learn how to cope with such issues as: preteen angst, tantrums, outright defiance, whining, laziness and self-motivation. The course will also instruct the Vault Overseer on how to draw up Behavioral Contracts (Form VT-BC0987891A/7) and define consequences for preteens who breach outlined obligations.

entries.title: VTU-PDM222
entries.text:
VTU-PDM222 - Puberty in Confined Environments

Many young Vault dwellers will reach the puberty stage during their preteen years. This course will enable the Vault Overseer to understand the changes that are occurring in these budding youths and become their mentor if necessary.

Explanation of physical and psycho-social behavioral changes is covered in the course as well as how to explain these changes to preteen dwellers in a way they'll understand. Also included will be how to properly administer and explain the Vault-Tec Puberty Welcome Kit (or V.T.P.W.K.) which should be presented to all preteen dwellers once they've achieved this growth milestone.

entries.title: VTU-PDM401
entries.text:
VTU-PDM401 - Preteens in the Workforce

Although a preteen can range from only 10-12 years of age, they certainly qualify for a variety of jobs in the average Vault. This course is specifically designed to explain the difficulties of various tasks, and which ones are optimal for the preteen dweller.

The course also deals with occupational safety considerations when assigning preteens to tasks involving nuclear, biological or chemical environments.

items.name: Employee Terminal

location.text: Found near White Powder Winter Sports.

items.lead: A terminal you can read in the world.

entries.text:
Ever since the attacks, I've been running. I didn't know where I was going, but I knew I had to get away. I wandered aimlessly for almost a week until I stumbled cross the remains of this store and decided to make it my home.

Almost everything of value here was gone, but at least it put a roof over my head. I was happy to see that the store had a fireplace, which I desperately needed to fight off the mountain chill. It was the first time since the bombs hit I got a decent sleep.

Using the store as a base camp, I've spent the last several days exploring the surrounding area and gathering supplies. I have yet to meet anything alive out here apart from wildlife, which has been sparse at best.

I heard some type of aircraft pass overhead, but by the time I ventured outside, it was gone. I'm beginning to think I am one of the few that's survived the attacks.

I returned to my home today to find two men stealing my supplies. I don't know who they were, but I couldn't afford to let all my hard work go to waste. I would have tried to reason with them, but they didn't look like the reasonable types. As soon as their hands were full, I opened fire. They never stood a chance.

I hope I haven't made a huge mistake.

I'm having trouble sleeping again, only taking small one-hour naps at best. Usually, I'm awakened by some distant gunshots or the cry of something unnatural hunting for prey.

Passing the hours in my new home has been a struggle. I've taken to staring at the pictures on the wall of people skiing and inventing stories of what their lives must have been like. It's hard to believe life was once that simple.

Had another pair of thugs try and raid my shelter today, this time and man and a woman.

I was home at the time and I saw them coming, so I called out offering them a chance to run. They laughed and started shooting. I returned fire and took down the man, but a shot from the woman caught me square in the shoulder. Fortunately, my gunfire chased her off, but I have a feeling she'll be back.

The wound in my shoulder is far worse than I expected. I don't have antibiotics, and I can't remove the bullet. Even lifting my arm has become difficult. If I don't get medical attention soon, I'm in serious trouble.

The only options I have are to abandon my shelter and seek help, or stay put and hope for the best. Both of those choices lead me to believe I'm not going to last very long.

My right arm is useless and I'm burning up with fever. I'm too weak to try and hunt for food or gather fresh water, which means I'm done for. My window of opportunity for seeking help is gone. 

This will undoubtedly be my last entry. If anyone discovers these messages and you find my body, all I request is some sort of proper burial. I hope my meager collection of supplies will help you more than it helped me. Good luck to you. Good luck to all of us.

transcript.text: I saw him... we were at this bar. The Wayward. Just north of Flatwoods.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: And what does he know?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: He said he was on the trail of this vault.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: The people kind or the riches kind?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: The kind that holds stuff.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: The kind that holds stuff. I'll consider the topic clarified. You think it's the treasure?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: I don't know. He-he didn't say.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: Well, seems like that'd be worth finding out, wouldn't it?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: Y-yes?

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: Are you afraid of me?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: Oh god yes.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: Don't be. We're not monsters here. We're pragmatists. You can get off the floor.

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: Are you--you're not going to kill me?

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: Not unless you give me a reason. Do you have a place to go?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: N-no.

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: Do you want one?

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: ... w-what would you need me to do?

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: Go upstairs. Have a meal and a drink, share what you know. Maybe it'll jog some memories. From there... we can talk.

transcript.speaker: Settler
transcript.text: And if I wanted to leave?

transcript.speaker: Roper
transcript.text: We're all free men and women here. A little family. We take care of our own, rest of the world... be damned.

items.name: Charleston Herald Exclusive: The Motherlode

location.text: Found near Charleston Herald, Sugar Grove.

items.lead: A holotape lying in the world — it can also come from a quest.

transcript.speaker: Bill Breyer
transcript.text: I'm William Breyer, investigative reporter for the Charleston Herald.

transcript.speaker: Bill Breyer
transcript.text: I'm currently standing just outside the security fencing of one of several Hornwright Industrial sites that have cropped up around the area in recent months.

transcript.speaker: Bill Breyer
transcript.text: I'm here tonight to try and get some answers about what has become known in certain circles as "The Motherlode project."

transcript.speaker: Bill Breyer
transcript.text: Could this be the answer local mining families have been looking for? A series of new mining projects that could reinvigorate the local economy?

transcript.speaker: Bill Breyer
transcript.text: Or, as environmental groups have suggested, could these be a fresh set of toxic disposal sites, poisoning the ground beneath our feet?

transcript.speaker: Bill Breyer
transcript.text: At the very least, according to local experts, the area's recent increase in seismic events can almost certainly be tied to these sites.

transcript.speaker: Bill Breyer
transcript.text: And now I'm here to see for myself what's really going on.

transcript.speaker: Bill Breyer
transcript.text: I've just made my way up to a small gap in the first line of fencing. The security here is intense. Barbed wire. Armed guards. Feels like a warzone.

transcript.speaker: Bill Breyer
transcript.text: I'm making my way over a small ridge and I--

transcript.speaker: Bill Breyer
transcript.text: Mother of god... the ground's shaking and-- oh my god... what is that?

transcript.speaker: Hornwright Worker
transcript.text: Hey! You! This is private propert-- Shit, it's that reporter. Jesus! He's got a gun!

transcript.speaker: Bill Breyer
transcript.text: Gun? Wait, this isn't a --- ah! Ah....

items.name: Colton Pickins's Police Report
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Officer Walton
transcript.text: This is Deputy D.B. Walton. Interview started at 3:35AM.

transcript.speaker: Officer Walton
transcript.text: All right, Mr. Pickins. Tell me everything that happened by starting from the beginning.

transcript.speaker: Colton Pickins
transcript.text: I was out behind my hotdog stand taking out the trash when I saw a light shining from the woods.

transcript.speaker: Colton Pickins
transcript.text: At first I thought it was a hunter with a flashlight, but then the light started... changing.

transcript.speaker: Officer Walton
transcript.text: Changing? How?

transcript.speaker: Colton Pickins
transcript.text: Well, the light started turning different colors.

transcript.speaker: Colton Pickins
transcript.text: First it was blue, then green, then red, then back to blue. Or wait, maybe it was green, blue, red. No, actually, it's red, blue...

transcript.speaker: Officer Walton
transcript.text: Yep, we get it. What happened next?

transcript.speaker: Colton Pickins
transcript.text: I suddenly got real dizzy, and I dropped the trash bag I was carrying. Next thing I knew, I was on the ground. .. I don't even remember falling.

transcript.speaker: Colton Pickins
transcript.text: I looked up, and that's when... that's when I saw it.

transcript.speaker: Officer Walton
transcript.text: "It?" Can you be more specific?

transcript.speaker: Colton Pickins
transcript.text: It was a man, but it also wasn't a man. It had gray skin and these huge black eyes. And, and it was wearing like a spacesuit or something.

transcript.speaker: Colton Pickins
transcript.text: What was really weird was that it wasn't saying anything, but I could hear it anyway. In my mind.

transcript.speaker: Colton Pickins
transcript.text: It told me to follow it onto its spaceship.

transcript.speaker: Officer Walton
transcript.text: Sigh. "The Flatwoods Monster," again?

transcript.speaker: Officer Walton
transcript.text: All right, I've heard enough. Colton Pickins, I'm arresting you for drunk and disorderly conduct and indecent exposure.

transcript.speaker: Colton Pickins
transcript.text: Indecent what? What are talking about? I didn't do anything wrong!

transcript.speaker: Officer Walton
transcript.text: Colton, we found you on the roof of your shack, buck naked, yelling at the top of your lungs.

transcript.speaker: Officer Walton
transcript.text: Your blood alcohol was .23 and it took four deputies to get you into handcuffs.

transcript.speaker: Officer Walton
transcript.text: We all go on a bender now and then, but you need to keep it at home.

transcript.speaker: Colton Pickins
transcript.text: What? No! Come on! You have to believe me.

transcript.speaker: Colton Pickins
transcript.text: The monster MADE me drunk, it... it was experimenting on me! Controlling my mind!

transcript.speaker: Colton Pickins
transcript.text: When are you people going to do something about the Flatwoods Monster?! It needs to be killed!

transcript.speaker: Officer Walton
transcript.text: I've had enough. Just get him out of here.

transcript.speaker: Officer Walton
transcript.text: This is Deputy D.B. Walton. Interview terminated.

items.name: History of Morgantown: Vol. I
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: This is Alisha Parker speaking, valedictorian of the last graduating class of Vault-Tec University.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: I believe it is my duty to record the events of Morgantown's final days for future generations.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: With any luck, someday a dweller from 76 will find this and know what happened here.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: After the bombs, Morgantown was a hellhole. Everything was on fire or dead.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: I don't remember much to be honest. A few of us hid inside the University but rations forced us out after a few weeks.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: When we emerged, we found ourselves in the perfect real-world scenario for exercising all the training we acquired at VTU. Yeah. Lucky us.

items.name: History of Morgantown: Vol. II
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: Some of the kids with Overseer training took the lead. And a few of the Greek houses started communities.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: I don't even remember what they were called.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: The largest of them, Kappa something something, started absorbing the smaller houses and slowly expanding their territory.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: If the world wasn't over, I might have found it interesting how feudalism was reimagined against the backdrop of nuclear war.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: We lost a lot of students in the first year. Some to radiation poisoning. Others to typical things like hunger and thirst.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: One kid was attacked by a large rat in the VTU courtyard, but we never found it. But we mostly lost kids to the House wars.

items.name: History of Morgantown: Vol. III
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: The RadAway shortages were terrifying.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: Some guys were fighting over a cache they found in a nearby pharmacy, and things got heated. They drew their guns and fired.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: The first student death by a fellow peer was recorded. This was the new Morgantown.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: The two biggest houses are the Roof House and the Street House -- named after the territories they control.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: A great student war unfolded -- but this wasn't the cute kind of hazing ritual known by VTU students. This was life or death.

items.name: History of Morgantown: Vol. IV
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: Without RadAway, the effects of intense radiation were already taking their toll.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: Kids were falling over dead, their hair and skin were falling off.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: Only the most powerful student houses were able to keep order among their ranks.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: This was only possible by eradicating the smaller groups of student survivors and stealing their supplies.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: Every dose of RadAway kept the powerful elite at the top of the food chain.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: Even now, I'm in hiding. On a roof somewhere far away from most of the other kids.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: There's one guy on the roof next over that I sometimes talk to, but we usually keep to ourselves to not attract attention.

transcript.speaker: Alisha Parker
transcript.text: I think his name is Victor.

transcript.text: And no, for anyone snooping in, the irony that I'm recording this rant is not lost on me.

transcript.speaker: Bookstore Owner
transcript.text: I can still mourn for the death of my favorite pastime without getting left behind in the past, thank you very much.

items.name: Interloper
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Lane
transcript.text: There are other things in this world now that cannot be explained. The end of the world has awoken... something.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Lane
transcript.text: We all know the Mothman is out there, stalking and watching us, but what of the unseen.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Lane
transcript.text: There are things we can only glimpse in our minds, great entities, beyond our comprehension.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Lane
transcript.text: The Mothman is a creature, more like us than the unknowable horrors in the peripheral vision of our subconscious minds.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Lane
transcript.text: No longer just a false memory now... I have heard a tale... of this entity made real, deep in the earth.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Lane
transcript.text: The story teller was mad by any reckoning, but his story no less true.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Lane
transcript.text: My name is Jeff Lane, and I will lay bare this...watcher. No matter how deep I must go, I will come to know the true nature of the interloper.

items.name: Jamey's Journal - November 2

location.text: Found near New River Gorge Resort.

items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Jamey
transcript.text: Dad's gone outside...He's gone outside...

transcript.speaker: Jamey
transcript.text: Tracy and I can't see him from the windows. We're not supposed to look anyway. Whatever was screaming out there...Well...we don't know what it is.

transcript.speaker: Jamey
transcript.text: I think it was coming from the pool.

transcript.speaker: Jamey
transcript.text: Mom said that Dad had to go looking for the other campers. If they're still alive, they might have food.

transcript.speaker: Jamey
transcript.text: ...I guess they could have food either way.

items.name: Kelly's Holotape
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Kelly
transcript.text: Hey Anya, I know we're just supposed to leave useful things in the dead drop so we don't take up a lot of space, but I wanted to tell you something.

transcript.speaker: Kelly
transcript.text: You're so practical and thoughtful, and you always notice the good stuff first and you always give me things so I can make it out here.

transcript.speaker: Kelly
transcript.text: You're really special to me. I'm sorry if this makes you mad to hear, you probably don't like me like that.

transcript.speaker: Kelly
transcript.text: I know I was a grade behind you when the war happened. I guess we have to take chances now though, right?

transcript.speaker: Kelly
transcript.text: I'll wait for you in the big cabin where we stayed during the field trip and maybe we can talk about it, okay?

items.name: Live-fire Training Exercise
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Dave Strauss
transcript.text: Sutton... I grew up here. Seems kind of quiet and lonely now.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Well it ain't as lonely as you think. This place crawls with ferals, an' ferals is why we're here, rook. It's time for some live-fire training.

transcript.speaker: Dave Strauss
transcript.text: Ferals?! Those things give me the willies! All that hissin' and raspin' and jumpin' around... but then you remember they used to be folks like us.

transcript.speaker: Dave Strauss
transcript.text: Oh no! What if some of them are my relations? Or, I mean, they used to be.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Hey! Get your head in the game, rook! Quit makin' these things out to be more than they are.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Well all come from around here, an' we all had families an' homes that we lost when the bombs fell. Sutton's just a place. The airport's home now.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Get ready. I'm going to make some noise an' draw them out. Just remember your trainin' an' you'll do fine.

transcript.speaker: Dave Strauss
transcript.text: Oh lord, please forgive me if any of these things is a cousin.

items.name: Lucky Hits! Lottery Recording
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: Dear Mr. and Ms. Bennett Orwell...

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: We, of the West Virginia "Lucky Hits!" Lottery Company, are pleased to inform you of the result for our November lottery game

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: held on the 10th of this month!

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: Your names are attached to "Lucky Hits!" lotto ticket '59-28-42-88'.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: We are overjoyed to tell you that this ticket was November's lucky lottery winner!

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: It's the largest single-month game in 'Lucky Hits!' history!

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: You are hereby approved to receive an immediate cash payment, in the amount of 300,000 dollars!

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: Mr. and Ms. Orwell, CONGRATULATIONS!

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: A local "Lucky Hits!" prize representative will be arriving at your residence on November 30th - just a few short days away!

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: To avoid any unnecessary mix-ups, please contact our headquarters as soon as possible, to confirm your home address!

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: We advise that it's in your best interest to keep this news from the public's attention.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: We value all of our "Lucky Hits!" customers, and we can't wait to hear from you!

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: Once again, CONGRATULATIONS, Mr. and Ms. Orwell: Winners of West Virginia's largest ever lottery game!

items.name: Lugnut's Vehicle Modifications
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Lugnut
transcript.text: So I finally found a super charger for Roper's Limo. I sent Dogbreath and his crew over to Gorge Junkyard and they hit the jackpot.

transcript.speaker: Lugnut
transcript.text: They even found an engine hoist, some big block double hump heads and pistons. The head gaskets are blown but that shouldn't be a problem, I'll know more when I start ripping it apart.

transcript.speaker: Lugnut
transcript.text: I'm also gonna take a shot at modifying the exhaust and suspension. The big rig is next on the list, though.

transcript.speaker: Lugnut
transcript.text: I'm having spikes welded on to the sides, that should save bullets when dealing with ghouls. I just finished up mounting a harpoon gun on the hood.

transcript.speaker: Lugnut
transcript.text: Can't wait to own some Settlers with that thing. The Radicals will rain hell on this earth once these vehicles hit the road.

items.name: Madigan Scouting Report - Garrahan
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: You don't mind if I record?

transcript.speaker: Hank Madigan
transcript.text: You're captain, Melody. Don't need my permission.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Hmph. So, how's it look out there, Hank?

transcript.speaker: Hank Madigan
transcript.text: Well, I found some more survivors. Started shooting at me the second they saw me, like the rest.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Sounds about par for the course. Seems there's not a sane mind south of Mount Blair. Anything else?

transcript.speaker: Hank Madigan
transcript.text: Ash is piling up faster than we expected.

transcript.speaker: Hank Madigan
transcript.text: But going by the maps the earlier teams did, it at least doesn't seem to be spreading anymore.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: So we've only lost Welch, Beckley, Lewisburg and everything around 'em. Little blessings, I suppose.

transcript.speaker: Hank Madigan
transcript.text: Oh. And actual good news. Garrahan Mining.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Been a long time since I've heard "good news" and "Garrahan Mining" said back to back.

transcript.speaker: Hank Madigan
transcript.text: No kidding. But that Excavator armor they made. Ruined the company? Rumor is it's tough as nails, and they've still got the plans on site.

transcript.speaker: Hank Madigan
transcript.text: Could you imagine what a patrol would be like if we could figure out how to make those things?

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Locals would hopefully be a lot less inclined to shoot first.

transcript.speaker: Hank Madigan
transcript.text: Bingo. You give me a day or two, I can head back down there, see what I can do.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: No. Garrahan can wait. You need rest. Head up to Morgantown. That Excavator armor'll still be there. Now go.

items.name: Magnus Westbrooke's Holotape
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Magnus Westbrooke
transcript.text: When DuBois dropped me off at Bolton Greens, I was horrified.

transcript.speaker: Magnus Westbrooke
transcript.text: Fourth in line for the Westbrooke fortune, and Momsy and Pa-pa had the nerve to leave me at a glorified daycare center while they travel the world?

transcript.speaker: Magnus Westbrooke
transcript.text: Ridiculous.

transcript.speaker: Magnus Westbrooke
transcript.text: To make matters worse, I'm forced to hobnob with the other children, some of whom are mere... millionaires. Ugh, the thought makes my skin crawl.

transcript.speaker: Magnus Westbrooke
transcript.text: The only saving grace of this prison is that they employ a sommelier in the dining room.

transcript.speaker: Magnus Westbrooke
transcript.text: Well, it's time to go fox hunting again. Oh drat, I appear to have scuffed my ostrich jodhpur boots.

transcript.speaker: Magnus Westbrooke
transcript.text: I suppose I'll have to use the... ugh, calfskin ones instead.

items.name: Melody Larkin: Dispatch
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: It's been a helluva week, I tell ya. We lost more good people fightin' off those damn scorched things again.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Now I got Chavez tellin' me we're pickin' up a new radio signal. Someone askin' for help.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: She wants me to take my team and follow it 'til we find 'em. Can't be too far. Already tracked it gainin' strength South a' here.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: Problem is, we'd have to go straight on through Raider country to find 'em and I don't have the time or men to spare right now.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: So, I hate to say it, but I gotta tell her it ain't gonna happen. Not now.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: My team's the last line of defense, and if I take 'em on some wild goose chase, we're leavin' ourselves open for another Christmas Flood situation.

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: And, you can bet your ass I ain't gonna let that happen again, even if it means someone out there might need us. Man alive, times 've changed.

items.name: Message to Beckley
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: JayDeedee
transcript.text: Testing... testing... This is Jay DeeDee. Hope this piece of junk is finally recording.

transcript.speaker: JayDeedee
transcript.text: Can't believe I'm using one of these contraptions to send a simple message, but you asked for an update, Earnest. So here you go!

transcript.speaker: JayDeedee
transcript.text: Gad is a goldmine! The town that was here may have been gone for ages...

transcript.speaker: JayDeedee
transcript.text: ..but between what they left and the gear from the last batch of muck farmers, I could be here for a long while digging it up.

transcript.speaker: JayDeedee
transcript.text: There's barely a trickle of water after the dam busted and there are riches poking out of the mud all over the place!

transcript.speaker: JayDeedee
transcript.text: I've already built a home of my own. It isn't much, but I'm trying to claim my spot before scavengers show up looking to pounce on the goods.

transcript.speaker: JayDeedee
transcript.text: That's why I need your help, Earnest.

transcript.speaker: JayDeedee
transcript.text: I know you got guys looking for work over in Beckley. Heard about those machines taking jobs from hard working miners.

transcript.speaker: JayDeedee
transcript.text: Tell whoever will listen that I am offering twice what they were making hauling coal to come up to New Gad and lend a hand.

transcript.speaker: JayDeedee
transcript.text: Oh! And whatever digging or mining gear they've got would be great too.

transcript.speaker: JayDeedee
transcript.text: Might need to bring some protection as well. Someone built a shack only a stone's throw away and it's only going to get more crowded.

items.name: Monorail Maintenance Log #30045
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.
items.contents: A terminal holotape: load it into your Pip-Boy or a terminal to read it.

items.name: Morris Stevens' Holotape
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Morris Stevens
transcript.text: Edie and I have been feeling a little extra hungry as of late, and the others are starting to ask questions.

transcript.speaker: Morris Stevens
transcript.text: "Morris, how can you be hungry when you're still so fat?" Well, you know what I say to that?

transcript.speaker: Morris Stevens
transcript.text: I'm hungry because I'm the boss here! It takes a lot of effort to wrangle these useless idiots so we don't all starve, and that works up an appetite!

transcript.speaker: Morris Stevens
transcript.text: Honestly, it's been several days since we've come across any more food. The usual unsuspecting travelers have been harder to come by.

transcript.speaker: Morris Stevens
transcript.text: I can only assume the damn Cutthroats have been scaring them all away, or not sharing their finds with us.

transcript.speaker: Morris Stevens
transcript.text: The others won't like it, but we're going to have to go to plan B. Edie's on board with me.

transcript.speaker: Morris Stevens
transcript.text: I've been thinking about Gregory. He's got a lot of meat on him, and he's been rather useless lately. No one will miss him.

transcript.speaker: Morris Stevens
transcript.text: Well, maybe his wife. And his little girl, perhaps.

transcript.speaker: Morris Stevens
transcript.text: But Vanessa will know what's good for her, and she's too much of a good fighter to eat just yet. And the kid... well, I'm not a monster.

transcript.speaker: Morris Stevens
transcript.text: Besides, kids are too scrawny.

items.name: Old Nate's Farewell
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Old Nate
transcript.text: I should be sitting here, lying about how I sacrificed myself for my so and so's and I'm quietly fading off and blah blah. I know the drill.

transcript.speaker: Old Nate
transcript.text: But look, I didn't choose to sit out here and watch the bombs go off in my bathrobe like some venerable old peach. No, I was left here to die because I'm old and mean and that's fine by me.

transcript.speaker: Old Nate
transcript.text: I like things how I like them, and I am not going to change one bit for anyone. I recorded this just in case anyone saw my body and felt bad for me.

transcript.speaker: Old Nate
transcript.text: To hell with your sympathy. I'm going out on an IV full of painkillers and you're just jealous that you didn't think of it first. Sucker.

items.name: Out of Time
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Really? You're going to record this?

transcript.speaker: Leo Chase
transcript.text: You're damn right I am! I want Madigan to hear about this when he gets back. I want him to know what you're trying to pull here!

transcript.speaker: Melody Larkin
transcript.text: You are way the hell out of line, Chase!

transcript.speaker: Leo Chase
transcript.text: I'm out of line?! I ain't the one agreeing to send the Fire Breathers on a suicide mission without our best man!

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: That's enough! Both of you, stop it!

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Look... Leo... the reports, they're talking about a horde of Scorched on the other side of those mountains.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: You know as well as I do that sealing the tunnel's our best chance to stop them. Maybe our only chance.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: If the Fire Breathers don't move now, everyone dies. It's just a matter of when.

transcript.speaker: Leo Chase
transcript.text: We just need more time! He's coming back. I'm telling you, he'll be here! We just... need time.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: We are out of time, Leo.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Melody's going to lead the mission. She's got experience in this kind of thing, and I'd trust her with my life. With all our lives.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Now turn off that damn recorder and do your duty, Fire Breather.

transcript.speaker: Leo Chase
transcript.text: Yes ma'am.

items.name: Psych Eval: Olivia P. Henderson
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.
items.contents: A terminal holotape: load it into your Pip-Boy or a terminal to read it.

items.name: Psych Eval: Wyatt Johnson
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.
items.contents: A terminal holotape: load it into your Pip-Boy or a terminal to read it.

items.name: Rita - The Fire Breather
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Buck
transcript.text: Hey Rita. So, right now, you're asleep, enjoying your last peaceful night's rest for God knows how long...

transcript.speaker: Buck
transcript.text: ... and I thought I'd record something for you to remember me by while you're locked away inside Charleston Fire Department...

transcript.speaker: Buck
transcript.text: ... training for the prestigious opportunity to dive face first into a bunch of mine fires with the rest of those Fire Breather nut jobs.

transcript.speaker: Buck
transcript.text: Heh. Honestly, though... ain't no Responder alive who's a better pick for that crew than you.

transcript.speaker: Buck
transcript.text: Just make sure you don't forget the basics with all this fancy new training. Always check your seals. It's stop, drop, then roll. The order's important.

transcript.speaker: Buck
transcript.text: And, most important, don't come back all crispy. Because I love what I'm looking at right now.

items.name: Sam Blackwell Interview, Pt. One
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: All right. It's recording. Thank you again for reaching out to me. I can't tell you how shocked I was to find out your letter was the real deal.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: Of course, Ms. Carter. I hope the trek wasn't too arduous.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: It was ... an experience. Not a lot of my interviews start with a bag over my heard. Just glad it didn't end up being a prank, I suppose.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: I apologize for that. Maintaining a low profile is a requirement for us now.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: And why is that, Senator? Why did you leave your position so suddenly?

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: Leaving was the only way I thought I'd be able to protect my family, Ms. Carter.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: But I've since realized that I'd left a lot of other people I care about in grave danger. I was hoping you could help me correct that.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: What are you talking about Senator?

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: There are sinister forces at work in the halls of government.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: I and my fellow members of the Free States will no longer be shackled to the putrefying corpse of this nation.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: Nor should anyone who values their lives. There is only one recourse left for the people of the United States: strike out on your own.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: Take whatever you can carry, get off the grid and get there fast. The end is coming, Ms. Carter.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: And when it does, your government has no interest in keeping you safe.

items.name: Sam Blackwell Interview, Pt. Two
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Sinister forces? The end is coming? Senator, you're making some big claims here. Do you have evidence to back it up?

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: This is not some doomsday fever dream, if that's what you're asking, Ms. Carter. I received my information from reliable sources, yes.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: And I'm just supposed to take your word for it?

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: You're going to have to, Ms. Carter. I'm trying to save lives, not put more at risk by exposing my sources.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Senator, I'm not trying to be rude here, but it sounds like you're trying to start a panic, and without evidence, I'm not willing to be a part of that.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: I also have it under the strictest confidence that you've been seen making multiple visits to a certain Charleston neurologist as of...

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: My health is not the issue here, Ms. Carter! These are peoples' lives!

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: The Executive branch, captains of industry, the Department of Agriculture! I peeked into their world and they threatened my life! My daughter's life!

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: We're just pawns to them! And the only way we survive ... is to step off the board. All I'm asking ... is that you share that message.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: ... I, I meant no offense. You just have to know how this looks from my end.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: I, I understand. It's just a ... sensitive topic.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Would you mind if I asked you one last question?

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: If it means you'll get the word out, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: You never resigned as Senator. Is that something you're planning to do?

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: I am. Consider this interview my formal resignation. Spread the word, Ms. Carter. All I ask is that my warning goes with it ... and nothing else.

transcript.speaker: Sam Blackwell
transcript.text: Now, if you wouldn't mind. My daughter and I have a lot to do. We're on our own out here, after all.

items.name: Sanjay's Report
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Sanjay Kumar
transcript.text: Sanjay's log: Tygart Water Treatment.

transcript.speaker: Sanjay Kumar
transcript.text: Where to begin. This place is so far gone. I mean... how? It's not like this building got nuked or anything.

transcript.speaker: Sanjay Kumar
transcript.text: Was this place run by animals? Are people that incompetent?

transcript.speaker: Sanjay Kumar
transcript.text: We've got fully corroded purifiers, filters, unused mind you, covered in some... black sludge.

transcript.speaker: Sanjay Kumar
transcript.text: Maria's not going to be happy about this.

items.name: Speaker Poole Interview
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Speaker Poole! Wait! Please just a moment of your time!

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: Just what I need... I'm sorry, don't have time right now Ms. Carter.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Are we still looking for Governor Evans? Is it true that Holbrook is the acting Governor?

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: No. The line of succession clearly states that the Speaker out ranks the Majority Whip.

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: Look, I don't have time for-

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Is it true that a mob of zombies attacked the southwestern check point?

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: What? What foolish-

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: No. It was people affected by the radiation. There's a passel of them over in the medical center.

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: Poor souls...

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Has there been any word from Washington yet, ma'am? Are we still at war?

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: What about the mutations? And the reports of the people seeing the Mothman?

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: Okay, that's enough. The Herald used to be an upstanding paper and y'all'r fixin' to turn it into a rag.

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: This is a Closed Session. Marshall, see that our friend finds her way out.

transcript.speaker: Abigale Poole
transcript.text: Mothman... really.

transcript.speaker: Marshall Barber
transcript.text: You heard her. Closed Session. No reporters.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Dammit.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Fine. But there HAVE been reports of people seeing the Mothman.

transcript.speaker: Marshall Barber
transcript.text: Uh huh. Get out of here before I pull your press badge.

transcript.speaker: Quinn Carter
transcript.text: Okay... Okay! I'm going, you don't have to shove...

items.name: Stuck
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I feel like I'm losing my mind.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I can't leave this roof or I'll die.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: Alisha has stopped talking to me.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I have nothing to do but obsess over my work.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: *laughs* How is that even remotely sane? I'm cataloguing constellations and the world has ended.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I have officially lost it.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I know I have, because lately I've been resisting the temptation to go down to street level.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: There's roving bands of murderous kids. People who I used to help cheat on their exams, can you believe it?

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I got them an A- and now they want to beat me to death with a wrench for a bag of chips.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I wish I wasn't on this nightmare planet.

transcript.speaker: Victor
transcript.text: I wish I was somewhere else, somewhere out there in the stars.

items.name: Test Log 3-12-78-A14
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Test Log 3-12-78-A14

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Eyes appear glassy. Subject seems to be experiencing decreased blood pressure and heart rate.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: While this new solution appears to trigger a vasovagal response in subjects with a complimentary DNA structure, no other reversal.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: It's no good. I don't know how much of the mutations we've seen are from radiation and what is from the compound we'd been working on.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: I don't understand how Samson got clearance for aerosolize testing before we even completed lab trials.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Did we cause this... skin disease... or is it just a mutation. And what of those whose minds have degraded?

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Oh great. The breakers just went out. This winter is taking a toll on the lab. Guess I better get to fixing it before the plants freeze.

items.name: Test Log 9-23-77-A10
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Test log 9-23-77-A10.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Animal subject shows no marked increase or decrease in muscle mass.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: However, those in the flora lab have said that this test run showed an increase in growth by as much as 25%.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: We felt certain that, due to the component make up fo the solvent, it would have a marked effect on fauna as well...

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: ...but even the inclusion of a matching protein sequence into the solution the resultant distillate fails to show an increase in size or growth rate.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Whoa! Okay down... Hey, down! Jessie can you grab it? Aaah!

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Ugh. What was that about? Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Natalie Ingesson
transcript.text: Ancillary observation: The test subject seems to be strongly drawn to the solution. This bears further testing. Is it the similar protein sequence?

items.name: The Battle of Morgantown
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: We lost another group of freshmen today.

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: I ordered them to start scaling the escape ladders at nightfall but it was a trap.

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: The whole thing was covered in oil and the roof asses lit them all on fire.

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: And I can't keep doing this!

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: We keep trying to starve them out since we control the roads into and out of town, but somehow they keep finding food, man!

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: They've even started to throw their empty food boxes down on us as mockery.

transcript.speaker: Vanessa
transcript.text: How are they surviving up there? Where are they getting their supplies?

items.name: The Big Day
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: Wait, is that... you brought a holotape recorder?

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: Oh, um... yeah. There's something I wanted to document. Don't worry, it's nothing weird, I promise.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: Anyway, you asked where I like to go to be alone and think, and here we are.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: When I was a student at VTU, I always thought Summersville was one of the prettiest towns I'd ever seen. It was... quaint, you know? Old-fashioned.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: Now it's lost all of its charm for me. I just see a sad, decaying place filled with the ghosts of a forgotten world.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: What draws you here? Is it the silence?

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: The view, actually. You can see the floodlands perfectly from here.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: The mud flats? Why? There's nothing to see there. It's a ruin.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: Because I never want to forget how lucky I am to be alive.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: I volunteered for the mission to Pleasant Valley because I was bored and wanted some excitement in my life. I know, I was young and stupid.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: We weren't even an hour outside the city when we heard the blast from the dam. We looked on as the river washed half of Charleston away.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: I lost every friend I had on that day, and for a long time, I felt like it was unfair that I survived. Like I should have died with them.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: But that all changed on the day I met you, Amy. You gave me a reason to want to be alive.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: That's why I wanted to ask you...

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: Jeff, don't. I know what you want to say, but... now isn't the time. I don't know if it ever will be. I just can't think about that right now.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: It's not that I don't care about you, but I have my work on the environmental monitoring program, and you've got your duties to the Responders.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: People are counting on us to be selfless. To put their needs ahead of ours.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: I know, but part of rebuilding the world is... well, having families again, and I think that's an important responsibility, too.

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: Besides, why even bother trying to survive if there aren't things worth living for?

transcript.speaker: Jeff Nakamura
transcript.text: Look... if this is too soon for you, then I'll wait until you're ready. Just promise you'll tell me if you change your mind.

transcript.speaker: Amy Kerry
transcript.text: Okay. I promise.

items.name: The Christmas Flood
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: This is Maria Chavez speaking, and today is December 25th, 2092.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Once, in the world before the war, this would have been a joyous time to celebrate with loved ones. Now it's a time to reflect and to mourn.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: It was on this day ten years ago that we lost so much in the tragic event we call the Christmas Flood.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: I'm making this recording in the hopes of ensuring the flood and its victims are never forgotten.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: I suppose the story really begins in November of 2077, the month after the war.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Survivors from the Pleasant Valley Ski Resort sent a group to Charleston to ask for help and supplies. The city leaders turned them away.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: There was so much chaos and so much need back then, I suppose it was an impossible request to grant.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: The failure to secure help led to a change in leadership for the survivors at the ski resort.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: A cold and brutal man named David Thorpe took charge, and he shaped those people into something terrible.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: They took what they wanted by force and killed anyone that stood in their way.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Years later, Thorpe's girlfriend Rosalynn led a raid on Charleston. They were spotted early, and a fight broke out.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: A few of them escaped, but Rosalynn was injured and taken prisoner along with some of the other raiders.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: By then, the Responders were more or less running things in the city, and we were doing pretty well for ourselves.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: We felt confident we could confront the raiders on their home turf, so we sent a group up into the mountains to see if we could make a deal.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: We hoped we could get them to leave us alone if we agreed to release some of the prisoners. We were wrong.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: Thorpe had somehow got his hands on a mini-nuke, and he used it to blow the Summersville Dam on Christmas morning.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: We lost almost everything; our homes, our supplies and most of our friends and family.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: The days and weeks that followed were the hardest of my life, but somehow, we held together.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: We kept the idea of the Responders alive, even though there were only a handful of us left.

transcript.speaker: Maria Chavez
transcript.text: That's the story of the Christmas Flood. Tell your children, tell everyone you meet. Let's keep the memory alive for as long as we can.

items.name: Too Much Noise
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: I talked to Sheila yesterday about finding some food. She said she'd give me the info about a place if I grabbed some for both of us.

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: I agreed, and she pointed me to an old building nearby filled with machines that could make something she called "cream."

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: I never heard of it, but she promised that it tasted good and it would keep us both from starving.

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: According to her instructions, all I had to do was push a button and the machines would start cranking out bottles.

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: What she forgot to tell me was that it would be loud as hell and attract every creature in earshot.

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: It took everything I had to fight the things that swarmed the building. I barely made it out of there alive.

transcript.speaker: Samuel
transcript.text: If anyone finds this, tell Sheila that I'm keeping all of the damn bottles of cream. Next time, she can come get her own.

items.name: Where Am I?
items.lead: A holotape lying in the world.

transcript.speaker: Chem Addict
transcript.text: Mmmmm, yeah. Yeah, that's the good stuff. Yeahhh... I'm flying man, I'm flying! Oh wow, wow! I'm in a different planet, man! I'm in outer space!

transcript.speaker: Chem Addict
transcript.text: Guys, do you feel this? Do you feel this, guys? Guys? Huh, where did everybody... AAAAAH, WHAT THE HELL IS THAT??

transcript.speaker: Chem Addict
transcript.text: OOOH MAN, please tell me you see that? Guys, do you see that? Becky, there's a lighthouse there, right? Right Becky? Steve? Oh god! OH GOD!

transcript.speaker: Chem Addict
transcript.text: Stay calm man, stay calm. You're up too high, there's no water around, no boats around. It's not a lighthouse, you idiot. They don't build lighthouses on mountains.

transcript.speaker: Chem Addict
transcript.text: It's the chems, haha! The chems, of course! I'll just close my eyes, and when I open them... three, two, one... NO! OH NO! NO NO NO NO NO! Where am I? Where am I?? WHERE AM I??
